description:
Programme or Project Overview

Radboud University invites applications for a PhD position on transcranial ultrasound stimulation (TUS) and computational affective neuroscience, funded by the ERC HEART2ADAPT project. The doctoral project uses low-intensity focused ultrasound to modulate deep brain circuits - including the amygdala, striatum and dorsal anterior cingulate cortex - and combines these experiments with computational models of affective processing. The goal is to understand how non-invasive stimulation of deep affective circuits can change emotional and motivational states relevant to mental health.

The position is a salaried four-year doctoral appointment under the Dutch CAO-NU collective agreement, based in the Donders Institute for Brain, Cognition and Behaviour at Nijmegen, one of Europe's leading cognitive neuroscience environments. The doctoral candidate will run stimulation experiments, acquire and analyse neuroimaging and behavioural data, and develop computational models linking stimulation targets to affective outcomes, working within an ERC-funded team with dedicated technical support.

Candidate profile

Applicants hold a master's degree in neuroscience, psychology, biomedical engineering or a related field, with strong programming and data-analysis skills. Experience with neuroimaging, brain stimulation, computational modelling or psychophysiology is an advantage. Applications are submitted through Radboud University's online recruitment system with a CV, transcripts, references and a motivation letter, and shortlisted candidates are invited for interviews.

Highlights

  • ERC HEART2ADAPT-funded four-year PhD position
  • Transcranial ultrasound stimulation of deep brain circuits
  • Amygdala, striatum and dACC affective neuroscience
  • Computational modelling of stimulation effects
  • Donders Institute research environment in Nijmegen
  • Salaried employment under the CAO-NU agreement
